PullRequest.Title: tool calls in dropdown and thinking headers
PullRequest.Body:

1. all tools inside dropdown
2. updates header using chat title service
3. refactor chat list renderer parts stuff to not have a persistant state - state is handled per part.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new remote boundary, trigger conditions, per-section cardinality, and lack of cancellation are explicit in the changed code and its callers. Exact provider latency/quota impact varies, so severity is medium rather than high.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Language-model provider activations/resolution, remote model requests, streamed response bytes, and provider concurrency/quota
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is one full title-generation request per finalized thinking section unless it has exactly one captured title and no tools. Tool-containing sections always take this path; parallel chats create the same number of concurrent uncapped requests, and disposed parts do not cancel them.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excess network/model load and lower chat throughput through contention or rate limits; title work can continue consuming resources after the user switches sessions or the rendered part is disposed.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Finalization chose an extracted or generic title locally and made no language-model/provider request.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Finalization now calls generateTitleViaLLM for common cases (no captured header, multiple headers, or any tool invocation), resolves Copilot models, sends a chat request, consumes the full stream, and passes CancellationToken.None.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 335 introduces the provider chat request on thinking-section finalization; the deleted implementation completed the header synchronously from local state.
Findings.Title: Avoid a model request just to finalize each thinking header
Findings.Impact: A standard agent turn with thinking plus a tool now launches an additional remote model request after the main response. Rapid or parallel agent workflows fan this out per response, potentially competing with the user's next real chat request; navigation cannot stop already-started decorative title requests.
Findings.Evidence: `finalizeTitleIfDefault` reaches generateTitleViaLLM unless generatedTitle exists or there is exactly one extracted title with zero tools. `appendItem` increments toolInvocationCount, making every tool-containing section ineligible for the local path. `ILanguageModelsService.sendChatRequest` directly delegates to the provider, while the changed call uses CancellationToken.None and only checks disposal after consuming the entire response stream.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep finalization local using the extracted/fallback title. If generated titles are required, move them behind an explicit/deferred path and tie a CancellationTokenSource to the part/response lifecycle, ensuring at most one in-flight title request per response.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The raw-vs-prefixed mismatch and progressive update call path are explicit. The issue is limited to collapsed mode (fixedScrolling does not update the title while streaming), which affects prevalence but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Markdown parsing/rendering, DOM replacement, file-widget queries and retained widget/listener objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: In collapsed thinking mode, the extra work occurs once per progressive thinking update after a header is present, so it grows with the number of streamed chunks; headers containing inline file anchors also retain another widget registration per update until the content part is disposed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased main-thread CPU/GC and rendering work during streaming, with potential chat scrolling/animation jank on long reasoning streams.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous setter displayed the extracted label and then stored that same raw label in currentTitle. Subsequent updates with the same extracted header matched the guard and skipped title rendering.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The changed setter displays and stores `Thinking: ${title}` while updateThinking continues comparing the next raw extracted title against currentTitle. For a stable title such as `Plan`, `Plan !== Thinking: Plan` forever, so every update calls setTitleWithWidgets again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 446 assigns the prefixed `thinkingLabel` to currentTitle; before the diff, updateThinking assigned the unprefixed `label`, allowing its unchanged-title guard to succeed.
Findings.Title: Keep the raw title stable across streaming updates
Findings.Impact: With `chat.agent.thinkingStyle` set to `collapsed`, a normal multi-chunk reasoning stream repeatedly reparses and replaces an unchanged title on the UI thread. `setTitleWithWidgets` also scans anchors and registers widgets in the part-wide store, amplifying allocation/retention when a title contains a file link.
Findings.Evidence: `ChatListItemRenderer.renderChatContentDiff` calls `updateThinking` whenever progressively rendered thinking content changes. `updateThinking` extracts the raw header and skips only when it equals currentTitle, but this added assignment stores the prefixed display string. Each miss reaches `setTitleWithWidgets`, which invokes the Markdown renderer, replaces label DOM, queries anchors via `renderFileWidgets`, and registers any widgets against the long-lived part store.
Findings.Recommendation: Track the raw extracted title separately (or store the raw title in currentTitle) and add the `Thinking:` prefix only to the rendered value. Also dispose title-specific widgets when replacing the title rather than registering them for the full part lifetime.

Scenarios.Scenario: Progressively stream a thinking response while the thinking style is set to collapsed
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each progressive list-render tick diffs the response and synchronously calls ChatThinkingContentPart.updateThinking on the UI thread. The changed raw/prefixed title mismatch then reparses Markdown, replaces title DOM, scans anchors, and registers widgets before that render tick returns.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of incremental thinking-content updates after a stable bold header appears; effective work is one extra title render per changed chunk, not one per distinct title.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser/UI work is serialized on the main thread; progressive updates repeatedly add work to that same render path rather than running concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The MutableDisposable releases the prior rendered Markdown result, but the changed currentTitle value defeats unchanged-title deduplication. File widgets are registered in the part-wide store and survive title replacement until the whole part is disposed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the progressive-update caller, comparison mismatch, synchronous Markdown/DOM work, and disposal ownership are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The default style is fixedScrolling, so prevalence depends on users selecting collapsed mode. Stream length, title markup, and device speed determine exact frame cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated synchronous rendering and retention regression; submitted as a medium-severity finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Finalize a live thinking/tool section, or render a completed historical response that lacks generatedTitle
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Finalization itself does not await title generation, so the main response/render can continue; however, the header's generated title depends on provider resolution and the full model response stream, and this background work shares model/provider resources with subsequent user chat requests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Activate/resolve the Copilot language-model provider and fetch model metadata through selectLanguageModels; a missing fast model performs a second selector pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Normally one selector resolution per generated header, or two when copilot-fast is unavailable before falling back to gpt-4o-mini.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Thinking finalization performed no provider activation or model selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the main response-render critical path, but required before the decorative generated title can progress and consumes extension/provider capacity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a language-model chat request and consume its complete streamed response to generate a header.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per qualifying finalized thinking section, with no grouping across response rows or chats.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The title was selected synchronously from extracted text or a generic local fallback, with zero remote requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the completed answer's critical path but on the generated header path; competes for provider concurrency/quota with user-initiated model work and continues after navigation because it is uncancelled.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One title-generation attempt per finalized rendered thinking section after the local shortcut. Any section containing a tool misses that shortcut; old persisted responses lack generatedTitle, so rendering multiple such response rows can fan out attempts by the number of instantiated rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider resolution is sequenced per vendor by the language-model service, but the changed code has no shared limiter for sendChatRequest across response parts. Parallel chats/history rows can therefore create multiple title requests; CancellationToken.None leaves them running after disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A successful generatedTitle on the same content object skips future generation and is now serializable. There is no in-flight or negative cache; failures retry on a later reconstruction/finalization, and disposal before completion prevents the successful result from being stored.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: trigger conditions, caller finalization, provider delegation, request cardinality, and CancellationToken.None are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency, quotas, internal transport, and the number of simultaneously rendered historical rows vary. The per-section request and lack of cancellation are not uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out regression; submitted as a medium-severity finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render tool invocations inside the thinking dropdown under off, withThinking, and always modes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tool parts are constructed on the normal chat list render path and their existing DOM nodes are appended into the active thinking part. In always mode, a lightweight thinking wrapper is also created for tool-only responses.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tool invocations in a response after excluding MCP tools and confirmation-gated live tools; each invocation remains one rendered tool part.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering and DOM insertion are serialized on the UI thread. No changed subprocess, filesystem, database, IPC, or network operation is reached merely by regrouping the existing tool DOM.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rendered parts are retained by the row template as before. getLastThinkingPart scans backward for the active part; no separate cache or external lookup is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the render path and absence of a new expensive boundary; insufficient evidence for a separate material performance finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Responses with unusually many content parts increase backward-scan and DOM costs, but the scan often terminates at the recent active thinking part and the diff does not establish a realistic independent regression beyond title generation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: DOM regrouping mostly reuses tool work already performed, and plausible list-scan overhead is not demonstrated as material.

Scenarios.Scenario: Persist and reopen chat responses carrying generated thinking titles
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatModel.toExport now passes thinking items through with generatedTitle. This adds only a short string to normal response serialization; the actual storage boundary is outside the changed hunk.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of thinking parts with generated titles in the saved chat session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialization is synchronous collection mapping as before; no changed queue, limiter, or parallel boundary behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted successful generatedTitle values act as a warm cache on reopen and avoid regeneration. Existing histories and failed/disposed attempts are cold and take the model-request path when finalized during rendering.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the serialization shape and warm-cache effect.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Title lengths are intended to be concise, so added serialized bytes are small; persistence timing may affect whether a newly generated value reaches storage but does not establish another performance regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the small persisted field is not itself material, while cold-history request fan-out is covered by the model-request finding.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all eight changed files and traced chat streaming, tool grouping, finalization, model-provider boundaries, disposal, and persistence. Submitted two diff-caused performance findings: repeated synchronous title reconstruction on collapsed streaming updates and uncancelled per-section language-model requests for decorative headers.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
